question: Compare the magnetic field due to a short bar magnet at equal distances on its axial and equatorial lines. Obtain the ratio of their magnitudes and explain the difference in their directions.

options.A: $B_{\text{axial}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{r^3}$ and $B_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{2M}{r^3}$, so $B_{\text{axial}}:B_{\text{eq}}=1:2$; both fields are along the magnetic moment.
options.B: $B_{\text{axial}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{2M}{r^3}$ and $B_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{r^3}$. Thus $B_{\text{axial}}:B_{\text{eq}}=2:1$. The axial field is along the magnetic moment, whereas the equatorial field is opposite to it.
options.C: $B_{\text{axial}}=B_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{r^2}$, so their ratio is $1:1$ and their directions are identical.
options.D: $B_{\text{axial}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{2M}{r^2}$ and $B_{\text{eq}}=\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{r^2}$, so the ratio is $2:1$; both fields point opposite to the magnetic moment.
